title: Tsardom of Russia
capsule: The Tsardom of Russia was established when Ivan IV was crowned tsar in January 1547, giving the Muscovite realm a Byzantine-derived imperial title and ideology. Under Ivan IV the Terrible (r. 1547–1584) it conquered the Khanates of Kazan (1552) and Astrakhan (1556), opening Siberia to rapid Cossack expansion that reached the Pacific coast by 1639. The Time of Troubles (1598–1613) brought foreign occupation and dynastic collapse before the Romanovs restored order; the Sobornoye Ulozheniye law code of 1649 under Alexis formalized serfdom and shaped Russian society for two centuries. Peter I's victory in the Great Northern War and proclamation of the Russian Empire in 1721 ended this polity, transforming it into a Western-oriented absolutist empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Muscovite and Volga territories are documented by land surveys (pistsovye knigi) and administrative records; Siberian frontiers are known from yasak-collection routes and fort records, but effective governance extent is difficult to map precisely; overall confidence is moderate to high.
